access: Drives the owner's real Chromium (via the external OpenCode Browse MCP server + extension the owner installs). Navigation is fenced by the project's site allowlist (.forge/browse.json); acting verbs and hand-back require approval.
description: OpenCode Browse (item #55, adopted — not built): six fenced verbs plus the item #65 verify loop (verify_in_browser) over the owner's signed-in Chromium via its local MCP server. Setup: install Browse with its own installer, add the preset block from the README ('Browse connector') to connectors.json, then enable this connector.
name: Browse (OpenCode)

tools.description: Open a web page in the agent's Browse tab. NAVIGATION IS FENCED: the URL's host must be on the active project's Browse site allowlist (.forge/browse.json in the project folder) — an unlisted host is refused before the browser is touched. Only http/https URLs. AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE FIRST: when you have a choice of pages, open the authoritative source — the official docs, the official API reference, or the project's own repository — before a scraped copy, mirror, or summary. If sources disagree, the authoritative one wins.
tools.name: browse_open

tools.description: Read the current Browse page as a TEXT snapshot. Text is the default and the rule — the context window is small, so page reading is text; use browse_screenshot only when text cannot answer the question.
tools.name: browse_read

tools.description: Click an element on the current Browse page, by CSS selector.
tools.name: browse_click

tools.description: Type text into a field on the current Browse page (CSS selector + the text).
tools.name: browse_type

tools.description: Screenshot the current Browse page. ON DEMAND ONLY — page observation is browse_read's text snapshot; take a screenshot only when the text cannot show what you need.
tools.name: browse_screenshot

tools.description: Hand the browser tab back to the owner — a login, 2FA, payment, captcha, or anything needing human hands. This call waits at the owner's approval gate (desktop dialog or phone deck, no timeout); it runs only when the owner approves, and that approval IS their Continue. After the browser reports a wall, Browse stays HELD — every verb refuses — until this call is approved.
tools.name: browse_hand_back

reason.description: What the owner is being handed and why, e.g. 'payment wall at checkout — card details needed'

tools.description: Verify your own work in the browser (item #65, the verify loop): open a page, read it back as a TEXT snapshot, and save a screenshot under the project's .forge/artifacts/ for the owner. The target is a project-relative path to a page in this project — served from a throwaway loopback preview that exists only for this call (the one navigation exempt from the site allowlist: it serves only this project's files, only on 127.0.0.1, only while verifying) — or an http(s) URL, which must be on the project's Browse site allowlist (.forge/browse.json) exactly like browse_open. The result is text plus the saved screenshot's path; the screenshot is never attached as image data. Use it after building or changing a page, before calling the work done.
tools.name: verify_in_browser

target.description: Project-relative path to a page (e.g. 'index.html' or 'site/page.html'), or an allowlisted http(s) URL
